Preparation

Two things to get in place before you start building: your PCI DSS compliance and a sandbox account.

PCI DSS compliance

All merchants that accept payment cards are required to comply with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS). You can review and validate your PCI DSS compliance with a Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ). The type of SAQ you need depends on your integration method.

  • SAQ A

    Flow, Hosted Payments Page (HPP), Payment Links, or our Mobile SDKs.

  • SAQ D

    Our Full Card API with your own integration platform.

Sandbox account creation

Set up a test account so you can build and validate before going live.

  1. Use a company email address to create your test account at checkout.com/get-test-account.
  2. You will receive a welcome email from Okta with the activation link.
  3. Activate your account and reset your password.
  4. Log in to the Dashboard at dashboard.sandbox.checkout.com.
  5. Once logged in as the Owner user, go to Settings → Roles and permissions and click + New User to invite more colleagues.

Account-related issues: support@checkout.com

Payin

Accept payments from your customers — the payment lifecycle, integration options, and the tools around them.

Payment lifecycle

A payment moves through fraud checks, authentication, authorization, and capture. The diagram shows the full flow and where a payment can be declined, voided, or flagged.

Integration

Choose the integration that fits your PCI compliance level and your build.

Flow & Remember Me

Flow is a pre-built, customizable payment user interface that you can embed directly into your website. It enables you to accept payments using Checkout.com's global network of payment methods with a single integration. Try the live Flow demo ↗ or download the sample code (.zip).

The Remember Me feature enables customers to save their card details during checkout. The next time the customer shops at any merchant that has Remember Me enabled, we display their saved card details.

Store Card Solution

Use Flow to verify the customer's card, then securely store the validated card credentials for subsequent payments — such as recurring billing, subscriptions, and one-click checkout.

Full Card API

If your level of PCI compliance is SAQ D, you can request a payment using the card's full details. Checkout.com provides a collection of APIs that enable you to process and manage payments.

Mobile SDKs

Checkout.com offers back-end and mobile SDKs for Android and iOS.

Amount format

Our payment gateway determines the charge amount by the value and the currency in the charge request. The amount field in a payment request must be a non-zero positive integer — no decimals. Details here.

Account Name Inquiry (ANI)

To reduce fraud risk, you can validate a cardholder's name against the name held by their issuing bank using an Account Name Inquiry (ANI). ANI is a card verification service that works independently of the financial transaction.

Good practice

To improve acceptance rates and enhance risk control, Checkout.com requires merchants to provide the following information when submitting payment and/or payment session requests:

  • cardholder name
  • customer.email
  • customer.name
  • customer.phone (good to have)
  • billing.address.country
  • billing.address.address_line1
  • billing.address.city
  • billing.address.state (for US)
  • billing.address.zip (good to have)
  • risk.device.network.ipv4 or risk.device.network.ipv6
  • risk.device_session_id

Account Funding Transactions (AFTs)

Card schemes (Visa & Mastercard) have mandates to ensure that acquirers/merchants with specific MCCs are migrated to AFTs. CKO will help merchants apply for AFT enablement with schemes. To flag transactions as AFTs, follow the docs here.

APMs

Checkout.com provides a wide range of global Alternative Payment Methods (APMs), such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, and local payment methods. Contact our team for more information.

Dashboard

The Dashboard is your single source for monitoring and analyzing all your payments — key performance indicators, payment history, details, and analytics in one place. You can also manage Disputes, Reports, Settlements, and Risk strategies from the Dashboard.

Webhook

Checkout.com can send automated notifications when events related to your account occur. You can receive notifications using Webhooks or EventBridge for all event types.

Response code

A Response Code is a five-digit numeric code that indicates the status of the request. There are four types:

1xxxx
Approved

The request was successful.

2xxxx
Soft decline

The request was declined, usually by the issuer bank, though subsequent attempts may be successful.

3xxxx
Hard decline

The request was declined. Most hard declines require the issuer or cardholder to rectify the outstanding issue(s) before a subsequent attempt can be made.

4xxxx
Risk responses

The request triggered a risk response. The status depends on the action specified in your risk settings. Declined by Fraud Detection.

Fraud Management

Fraudsters specifically target new merchants during their first 30–90 days, assuming security models are not yet fully calibrated. Follow these pillars to protect your processing.

Mandatory 3D Secure (3DS)

Policy: All transactions must be processed with 3D Secure. 3DS adds an authentication layer that helps verify the cardholder's identity with the issuing bank. It is your primary line of defense against unauthorized card use and provides significant protection against fraud-related chargebacks.

Identity-to-Payment (I2P) Anchoring

Standard authorization responses do not return the cardholder's name. This allows fraudsters to pass KYC as "User A" but pay with a card belonging to "User B."

Account Name Inquiry (ANI)

Use ANI to proactively send the KYC-verified Legal Name to the bank for verification.

Execution

ANI can only be performed on a $0 Authorization. We recommend you implement this as a mandatory part of the transaction flow (e.g., during card onboarding or immediately before the first purchase) to ensure identity alignment before funds are captured.

Hard Block Policy

If the bank returns a "No Match" result for the name, the transaction should be automatically declined.

Device Intelligence

Risk SDK (Mandatory)

Regardless of your integration method, you must integrate the Checkout Risk SDKs on your front-end. It is the only way to track physical hardware IDs and spot professional "fraud farms" using multiple accounts on one device.

The "Cold Start" Risk Model

Protect your launch with temporary "Speed-Bumps" for new accounts:

  • Tiered Limits: Keep transaction caps low (e.g., $100) for a user's first week.
  • Withdrawal Holds: For high-liquidity assets (like crypto), implement a 24–48 hour hold on payouts for new users. This allows time for Early Warning (TC40) reports to arrive before the funds are gone.

Proactive Ratio Protection

Rapid Dispute Resolution (RDR)

Set automated rules to refund disputes instantly. This kills the dispute before it hits your chargeback ratio.

Webhook Automation

Configure your system to freeze accounts and cancel pending orders the moment a Fraud Reported (TC40 or SAFE) webhook is received.

Metadata

We recommend passing additional Metadata in your payment requests. This lets us and our risk team better monitor your traffic, identify more fraud, and cross-check against broader network patterns. Key fields with the most impact include:

Identity & KYC insights

  • kyc_level: (e.g., Tier_1 vs Tier_2) to flag high-value attempts from unverified users.
  • user_age: (Integer) physical age from ID — critical for spotting "Generational Fraud" (senior exploitation or young/mule activity).
  • account_age: (in days) crucial for spotting "hit and run" attacks.
  • is_first_purchase: (Boolean) keep true until the user has a successfully captured payment.
  • document_type: helps identify if a specific forged document type is being cycled through the platform.

Account integrity

  • email/phone_verified: (Boolean) fraudsters often use unverified or VoIP details.
  • total_successful_orders: helps us "green-light" your loyal, low-risk customers.
  • is_trusted_customer: (Boolean) your internal flag for high-reputation users (recommend 3+ successful payments over a 45-day window with consistent device/IP signatures).

Transaction context

  • asset_type: (e.g., BTC, USDT) helps us monitor liquidity-driven fraud trends.

Fraud Detection

Our Fraud Detection solution gives you the power to control what happens to the payments you process. Payments are assessed against the risk assessment rules that you set in Dashboard → Fraud - Strategy page. Contact us for a demo session.

Disputes Management

A dispute, or chargeback, occurs when a customer questions the validity of a transaction and contacts their bank (the issuer) to get a refund. The dispute process begins when a transaction is questioned by the cardholder, then goes through a number of stages before it is resolved.

You can easily manage disputes from Dashboard → Disputes.

FAQ

How can I check a transaction's status and why it failed?

You can find this in two places — the Dashboard and the API.

Dashboard: open the Payments page and search by payment ID. Hover over the response code to see the status, and open the payment details page for the full breakdown.

API: the same response code is returned in the API response for every payment request.

How should my finance team reconcile with Checkout.com?

Follow our reconciliation guide, which walks through matching settlements and payouts against your processed payments.

How do I submit a support ticket?

Sign in to the Dashboard, click the question-mark icon in the upper-right corner, and select Request support.

How do I create API keys?

Sign in to the Dashboard, select the Developers section in the left-side menu bar, click on Keys, and select Create a new key. See the Developers documentation for details.

How do I set up single sign-on (SSO)?

Configure SSO for your team from the Dashboard — follow the SSO setup guide.

How can I view and update my business details?

You can view and update your business details directly in the Dashboard. See Manage business details.

How can I retrieve reports?

Checkout.com provides a range of reports to support your business operations. You can retrieve them in four ways:

  • Generate and download reports in the Dashboard, on demand or on a schedule.
  • Retrieve reports programmatically using the Reports API.
  • Access reports over Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP).
  • Receive scheduled reports via webhooks.

See Retrieve reports for setup instructions.

Can I set up recurring payments?

Yes. You can charge a customer on a recurring basis using their stored card details — see Recurring payments with stored card details.

What should be on my pre-go-live checklist?

Before you switch on live traffic, confirm your technical integration and configuration are production-ready:

  • Activate the Dashboard: ensure your Dashboard is activated and the right people on your team have access.
  • Swap API keys and endpoints: move your environment configuration from sandbox to production. Replace all test public and secret keys with the live production keys generated in the Dashboard.
  • Configure live webhooks: recreate all system-critical webhooks in your live environment. Make sure your server listens for live events such as card_verified, payment_approved, payment_declined, payment_captured, payment_refunded, and payment_voided, and that your live endpoints are secured and authenticated.
  • Enable 3D Secure (3DS) and fraud rules: review your 3DS rules in the Dashboard. Confirm Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) is enabled and correctly configured for regions where it is mandatory (such as Europe) to avoid immediate issuer declines.
  • Configure reporting methods: set up your reporting channels (Dashboard, API, and SFTP) for financial reconciliation.
  • Ensure good data health: confirm sufficient information is passed on each request for strong data quality, and comply with AFT mandate requirements where applicable (optional).
  • Run a production smoke test:
    1. Process a real transaction. Buy a low-value live item using a real personal or corporate card. Do not use sandbox cards — they fail instantly in production.
    2. Verify the webhook response. Monitor your backend logs and confirm your system captures the live event and moves the order status from "Pending" to "Paid".
    3. Trigger a partial or full refund. Initiate a refund from your platform's backend or the Dashboard to confirm the reverse payment loop works end to end.
